title: Level 4 (Expert) - B-24
notes:
West leads the ♠K against 3NT. South should duck West's spade opening lead. When West continues spades it is safe to win the ♠A as East is marked with only 2 spades by West's weak 2 bid.

Only 4 club tricks are needed to make the contract. It may seem that South should guard against West having a singleton ♣K by playing the ♣A on the first round. Leading the ♣A play will not work when East has a singleton ♣K as West will have a certain club entry to cash his spades.

To guard against both possibilities, South should lead the first round of clubs from the dummy. South crosses to the dummy and leads a club. If East plays the ♣K, South ducks and the contract is safe.

If East follows low, South plays the ♣A, dropping the ♣K if it is singleton. If West follows low, South can return to the dummy and play clubs towards the closed hand. Notice that ducking the second round of spades will give East a chance to discard a singleton ♣K on the third round of spades. West will have a certain entry and the contract will be defeated.
